# Automations

Create and change automations, their schedules and their triggers, and fire one. Automations are known as automated actions in Maitento, which is why the calls start with `Action`.

**Library:** [Maitento](index.md#maitento), for apps. More in [Automations](../../../concepts/automations.md).

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`ActionCreate`](#actioncreate) | Creates an automation, with the actions it starts when it is triggered, and returns it. |
| [`ActionDelete`](#actiondelete) | Deletes an automation, with its schedules, triggers and history. |
| [`ActionGet`](#actionget) | Returns an automation: its actions, schedules, triggers and recent history. |
| [`ActionHistory`](#actionhistory) | Returns the runs an automation has started, newest first. |
| [`ActionList`](#actionlist) | Returns the automations in a namespace, or in your whole tenant. |
| [`ActionMsgTriggerAdd`](#actionmsgtriggeradd) | Adds a message trigger to an automation, so it starts whenever another run changes and matches a filter, and returns the automation. |
| [`ActionMsgTriggerDisable`](#actionmsgtriggerdisable) | Switches off, without removing it, one of an automation's message triggers, and returns the automation. |
| [`ActionMsgTriggerEnable`](#actionmsgtriggerenable) | Switches on one of an automation's message triggers, and returns the automation. |
| [`ActionMsgTriggerRemove`](#actionmsgtriggerremove) | Removes one of an automation's message triggers, and returns the automation. |
| [`ActionScheduleAdd`](#actionscheduleadd) | Adds a schedule to an automation, so it starts at the times a cron expression gives, and returns the automation. |
| [`ActionScheduleDisable`](#actionscheduledisable) | Switches off, without removing it, one of an automation's schedules, and returns the automation. |
| [`ActionScheduleEnable`](#actionscheduleenable) | Switches on one of an automation's schedules, and returns the automation. |
| [`ActionScheduleRemove`](#actionscheduleremove) | Removes one of an automation's schedules, and returns the automation. |
| [`ActionTrigger`](#actiontrigger) | Triggers an automation by hand: starts each of its actions now, and returns the id of the first run it started, without waiting for it. |
| [`ActionUpdate`](#actionupdate) | Replaces an automation's name, description and actions, and returns it. |

### ActionCreate

Creates an automation, with the actions it starts when it is triggered, and returns it.

```c
jsonObject ActionCreate(string namespaceName, string name, string description, string actionsJson)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `namespaceName` | `string` | The namespace to create it in. It is required: here `""` doesn't mean this app's namespace. |
| `name` | `string` | The automation's name: letters, digits, `_`, `-` and `.`, unique in its namespace. |
| `description` | `string`, can be empty | What it is for, in your own words. Pass `""` for none. |
| `actionsJson` | `string` | What it starts: a JSON array of actions, as text (a `jsonArray` works too). |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The new automation, as a JSON object.

It starts with no schedule and no message trigger: add them with [`ActionScheduleAdd`](#actionscheduleadd) and [`ActionMsgTriggerAdd`](#actionmsgtriggeradd), or run it now with [`ActionTrigger`](#actiontrigger). Every trigger starts each of its actions in turn.

Each action is `{ "name": "…", "config": { … } }`, and its `config` must start with `$type`: `app`, `interaction`, `interaction-message`, `capsule` or `codepipeline`. Set `$type` first when you build the object. An `app`, `interaction` or `capsule` action names the version it starts, as `"version": { "id": "…", "version": 1 }`, with its `inputs` as `[{ "name": "product", "value": "…" }]`; it keeps starting that version after you deploy a new one. A `codepipeline` action names its pipeline instead. The fields are those of an automation's actions in the API.

Fails with `Invalid actions JSON: …` when the text doesn't parse into actions, `At least one action is required` for an empty list, and when the name is taken or not a valid name, the namespace doesn't exist, or an action names something your tenant doesn't have or leaves out one of an app's inputs.

The automation is a JSON object: `id`, `name`, `description`, `actions` (each with its `id`, `name` and `config`), `schedules`, `messageTriggers`, `nextScheduledRunAt`, `history`, `totalExecutions`, `consecutiveFailures`, `lastExecutedAt` and `lastProcessId`.

### ActionDelete

Deletes an automation, with its schedules, triggers and history.

```c
void ActionDelete(guid actionId)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `actionId` | `guid` | The automation's `id`. |

Runs it has already started carry on. Fails with `Not found` when there is no such automation.

### ActionGet

Returns an automation: its actions, schedules, triggers and recent history.

```c
jsonObject ActionGet(string nameOrId)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `nameOrId` | `string` | The automation's `id`, or `name@namespace`. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The automation, as a JSON object.

Name it by id, or as `name@namespace`: unlike most calls, a name needs its namespace. Fails with `Action name must be in format 'name@namespace' or a valid GUID` for a name without one, and `Not found` when there is no such automation.

The automation is a JSON object: `id`, `name`, `description`, `actions` (each with its `id`, `name` and `config`), `schedules`, `messageTriggers`, `nextScheduledRunAt`, `history`, `totalExecutions`, `consecutiveFailures`, `lastExecutedAt` and `lastProcessId`.

### ActionHistory

Returns the runs an automation has started, newest first.

```c
jsonArray ActionHistory(guid actionId, int limit)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `actionId` | `guid` | The automation's `id`. |
| `limit` | `int`, can be empty | The most entries to return. Pass `""` for 50, which is also as many as are kept. |

**Returns** `jsonArray`: A JSON array of history entries.

Each entry is a JSON object: `triggerType` (`Schedule`, `Message` or `Manual`); `triggerId`, the schedule or message trigger that fired (null for a manual trigger); `actionId`, which of its actions; `processId` and `processType` (`App`, `Interaction`, `Capsule` or `CodePipeline`), the run it started (an all-zero id when it couldn't start one); `dateStarted`; `dateCompleted`; `outcome` (`Pending` while the run is going, then `Success`, `Failed` or `Killed`); and `errorMessage`, why the run couldn't be started (read the run itself for why it failed). An automation keeps only its newest 50 entries. Fails with `Not found` when there is no such automation.

### ActionList

Returns the automations in a namespace, or in your whole tenant.

```c
jsonArray ActionList(string namespaceName)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `namespaceName` | `string`, can be empty | The namespace to list. Pass `""` for every automation in your tenant: unlike most list calls, not only this app's namespace. |

**Returns** `jsonArray`: A JSON array of automations.

Each element of the JSON array is an automation as [`ActionGet`](#actionget) returns it. Fails with `Namespace '…' was not found.` when the namespace doesn't exist.

### ActionMsgTriggerAdd

Adds a message trigger to an automation, so it starts whenever another run changes and matches a filter, and returns the automation.

```c
jsonObject ActionMsgTriggerAdd(guid actionId, string triggerName, string triggerType, string eventFilter, bool enabled)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `actionId` | `guid` | The automation's `id`. |
| `triggerName` | `string`, can be empty | A name for the trigger. Optional: pass `""` for none. |
| `triggerType` | `string` | Which kind of run it listens to: `AppProcessUpdated`, `InteractionProcessUpdated` or `CapsuleProcessUpdated`, in any case. |
| `eventFilter` | `string`, can be empty | The JSONPath filter the change must match, as described above. |
| `enabled` | `bool`, can be empty | Whether it fires from now. Pass `""` for `true`. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The automation, as a JSON object. The new trigger, with its `id`, is the last of its `messageTriggers`.

The filter is a JSONPath expression over the change: the run is under `item`, with its status as a number (`5` is `Finished`), so `$..[?(@.item.status == 5)]` matches a run that finished. A trigger with no filter fires on every change of every run of its kind, including the runs the automation starts itself: always give one.

An automation has at most 10 message triggers. Fails with `Invalid trigger type. Valid values: …`, `Invalid JPath in EventFilter: …`, `Maximum of 10 message triggers per action is allowed`, and `Not found` when there is no such automation. The result is the automation, as [`ActionGet`](#actionget) returns it.

### ActionMsgTriggerDisable

|---|---|---|

### ActionScheduleAdd

Adds a schedule to an automation, so it starts at the times a cron expression gives, and returns the automation.

```c
jsonObject ActionScheduleAdd(guid actionId, string scheduleName, string minute, string hour, string dayOfMonth, string month, string dayOfWeek, string second, bool enabled)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `actionId` | `guid` | The automation's `id`. |
| `scheduleName` | `string`, can be empty | A name for the schedule. Optional: pass `""` for none. |
| `minute` | `string`, can be empty | The minutes field, such as `0` or `*/15`. |
| `hour` | `string`, can be empty | The hours field, in UTC, such as `7`, or `*`. |
| `dayOfMonth` | `string`, can be empty | The day-of-month field, such as `1`, or `*`. |
| `month` | `string`, can be empty | The month field, such as `1` for January, or `*`. |
| `dayOfWeek` | `string`, can be empty | The day-of-week field, such as `1-5` for Monday to Friday, or `*`. |
| `second` | `string`, can be empty | The seconds field, for a six-field expression. Pass `""` for none. |
| `enabled` | `bool`, can be empty | Whether it runs from now. Pass `""` for `true`. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The automation, as a JSON object. The new schedule, with its `id` and `nextOccurrence`, is the last of its `schedules`.

The fields make a cron expression, and times are UTC. `ActionScheduleAdd(id, "every-morning", "0", "7", "*", "*", "*", "", "")` runs the automation every day at 07:00 UTC; `"30", "9", "*", "*", "1-5"` is weekdays at 09:30, and `"*/15", "*", "*", "*", "*"` every 15 minutes.

Every field needs a value: pass `*` for "every". A blank field doesn't mean `*`, and makes the schedule invalid. `second` is the exception: pass `""` there for an ordinary five-field schedule.

An automation has at most 5 schedules. Fails with `Invalid cron schedule: …`, `Maximum of 5 schedules per action is allowed`, and `Not found` when there is no such automation. The result is the automation, as [`ActionGet`](#actionget) returns it.

Switches off, without removing it, one of an automation's schedules, and returns the automation.

### ActionTrigger

Triggers an automation by hand: starts each of its actions now, and returns the id of the first run it started, without waiting for it.

```c
string ActionTrigger(guid actionId)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `actionId` | `guid` | The automation's `id`. |

**Returns** `string`: The id of the first run it started.

The runs start as the user this app runs as, and the automation's history records them as `Manual`. They aren't children of this app run and don't use its model keys or settings: to start a child run, use [`AppStart`](apps.md#appstart) or [`InteractionStart`](interactions.md#interactionstart).

When some actions start and others can't, the id is that of the first run that started, and the failures are in [`ActionHistory`](#actionhistory). When nothing could start, it fails with `The automation '…' could not start: …`, giving the reason. Fails with `Not found` when there is no such automation.

### ActionUpdate

Replaces an automation's name, description and actions, and returns it. Its schedules and message triggers stay as they are.

```c
jsonObject ActionUpdate(guid actionId, string name, string description, string actionsJson)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `actionId` | `guid` | The automation's `id`. |
| `name` | `string` | The automation's name from now on. Pass the current one to keep it. |
| `description` | `string`, can be empty | The description from now on. Pass the current one to keep it, or `""` for none. |
| `actionsJson` | `string` | Every action it starts from now on: a JSON array of actions, as text (a `jsonArray` works too). |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The automation, as a JSON object.

The actions take the form [`ActionCreate`](#actioncreate) describes, and the list you give replaces the old one. A code pipeline action's credentials and repository secrets, which reading an automation never returns, are kept when you leave them out.

Fails with `Not found` when there is no such automation, and in the ways [`ActionCreate`](#actioncreate) does. The result is the automation, as [`ActionGet`](#actionget) returns it.
